rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only, single-profile model provides a useful performance baseline. config_001 tests this minimal setup using PCA, without aggregation, learned encoders, image features, or fusion, which helps isolate the effect of the basic RNA representation and profile setting. It is the best first experiment because it is simple, likely fast, and establishes a reference point for later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed run is an RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, so there is still no evidence that image features are informative. config_010 tests a simple image-only ResNet50 single-profile model to establish an image baseline and isolate the contribution of the image representation before adding multiprofile aggregation or fusion. This is the best next use of budget because it is minimal, directly reduces uncertainty about a top-level design choice, and creates clean comparisons for later multimodal experiments.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet, so RNA is the current promising branch, but it is unclear whether multiprofile aggregation can improve it. config_002 tests the simplest multiprofile extension of the best RNA baseline by adding multiple profiles with avgpool while keeping the same PCA representation and avoiding fusion or transformer complexity. This is a high-information next step because it clarifies whether profile aggregation matters before committing budget to more complex RNA encoders, transformer aggregation, or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is currently the strongest result (0.591 acc, 0.573 F1), clearly better than single-profile RNA and weak image-only ResNet50. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation improves over avgpool for multiprofile RNA. config_003 tests this with a minimal change from the best RNA setting, isolating the aggregation effect before spending budget on more complex encoder, image, or fusion choices.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002), clearly better than singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA under the same favorable multiprofile/avgpool setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200, keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed, so it directly isolates the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the best-known profile/aggregation choice, tests a high-impact design decision, and avoids confounding by adding fusion or changing aggregation simultaneously.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool: scvi_n200 reaches 0.650 accuracy / 0.628 F1, clearly above pca_n2000 under the same profile and aggregation setting (0.591 / 0.573), while transformer aggregation was weaker for pca. This experiment tests whether the alternative RNA encoder scgpt can match or exceed scvi_n200 in the currently best setting, isolating the effect of representation choice. It is a one-factor extension of the most promising configuration, has high expected performance, and will clarify whether encoder selection is the next important lever before adding image fusion.

The strongest completed result is config_005: RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool, with 0.650 validation accuracy and 0.628 F1. Existing evidence also suggests avgpool can outperform transformer aggregation for multiprofile RNA encoders, as seen with pca_n2000, but the scvi_n200 + transformer combination is still untested. config_006 tests whether transformer aggregation can improve the best current RNA-only multiprofile setup while changing only the aggregation choice. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction and directly isolates an important design decision before moving to more complex multimodal or fusion configurations.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently the strongest direction (~0.653 accuracy/F1), but image evidence is sparse: resnet50 image-only singleprofile is weak (0.208 accuracy, 0.172 F1). The key uncertainty is whether a stronger image representation can provide useful signal before committing budget to multimodal fusion. config_013 changes only the image encoder to ImageNet ViT-L relative to config_010, isolating the effect of image representation. If ViT improves image-only performance, it justifies testing multimodal ViT configurations; if not, it suggests the image modality may not be useful and budget should remain focused on RNA-side improvements.

RNA-only multiprofile models are currently strongest, especially scvi_n200 with avgpool/transformer around 0.65 validation accuracy, while image-only single-profile models are weak (ResNet50 0.208, ViT 0.227). The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can make the image modality useful before investing in many multimodal fusion configurations. config_014 directly extends the best single-profile image baseline by testing imagenet_vit_l with multiprofile and simple avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting/aggregation for image representations. This is the best use of the next budget because it is simpler than multimodal testing, reduces uncertainty about whether image features can contribute at all, and will inform whether multimodal fusion experiments are worth pursuing.

The strongest unimodal evidence is RNA scvi_n200 multiprofile, with avgpool at 0.650 accuracy/0.628 F1 and transformer at 0.653/0.628, while the best tested image setting is imagenet_vit_l multiprofile avgpool at 0.332/0.315. This experiment tests whether adding that weak but tested image representation to the best RNA representation via simple concatenation can improve over RNA-only. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest RNA direction, uses a multimodal combination whose RNA and image subsettings both have unimodal baselines under the same profile/aggregation, and directly clarifies whether multimodality helps before spending experiments on fusion variants or untested image aggregations.
